messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-8491 triggered: 'watchdog-synth us-west-2 failure rate > 90% (5m)'. link: <http://ops.redwood/pd/PD-8491>
pagerduty: PD-8491 - triggered by synthetic-watchdog. severity: high. responders paged: #oncall.
alice: ack - oncall here, jumping in. what's impacted?
ben: checking dashboards now. seeing spike in failed canary responses, mostly 504s and empty bodies.
carla: any customer-facing errors? I see increase in API 5xx for text-generation routes in us-west-2 from ~2% to ~28% over the last 5m.
alice: ok, mark impact: partial degradation for us-west customers - elevated error rate + tail latency.
dave: can we fail traffic to eu as temporary mitigation? is smart-routing ready to flip?
ben: we can prefer eu-1 for new sessions. existing sessions sticky due to KV cache. need approval to run the change.
alice: approve. ben, go ahead.
ben: running command now:
```
rctl set-routing --service=synth-watchdog --prefer-region=eu-1 --dry-run=false
```
ben: applied. monitoring.
incident-bot: routing change applied by ben at 2026-03-14T09:24:12Z. PD-8491 note updated.
ben: for new requests failures are dropping in us-west, old sessions still failing (sticky KV behavior).
carla: digging into logs: model-variant fallback is failing due to KV cache version mismatch on wgpu nodes (v1.2.3).
emma: rolling restart of wgpu pool in us-west should clear stale caches. recommend 1-at-a-time.
dave: agree. schedule rolling restart with short drain.
ben: kicking restart:
```
infractl restart-pool --pool=wgpu-usw2 --parallel=1 --grace=30s
```
pagerduty: PD-8491 acknowledged by alice.
alice: I'm going to hand off to dave after the initial stabilization. dave, you're on.
dave: oncall ack, taking over. monitoring full timeline.
ben: first node restarted — error rate down to 6% from 28% (observed over 2m window).
carla: still seeing a small uptick on embeddings path in eu-1 (capacity bump from failover). watch for overload.
dave: can we put a temporary circuit-breaker on heavy embedding routes in eu to protect capacity?
ben: applying temporary rate cap now:
```
api-gw update-route /v1/embeddings --rate-limit=800r/s
```
incident-bot: rate limit update accepted and applied.
carla: quick impact check: top affected tenants = acme-corp (non-critical batch jobs), zoomlabs (dev), one enterprise test tenant. no major revenue-impacting customers flagged, but acme has time-sensitive runs.
alice: pinging account lead @sasha to inform acme support.
sasha: received. I'll send a short heads-up and offer mitigation steps.
emma: we should open an incident doc and assign owners — I'll start the postmortem doc.
dave: suggestion for follow-up: add a metric for KV cache version skew and include rollout gating to prevent mismatched variants.
ben: agreed, adding to infra backlog and will open PR to add rollout checks.
carla: ETA to fully resolve?
ben: after completing rolling restarts and failover stabilization we expect baseline in ~15-30m. will update if anything changes.
incident-bot: PagerDuty escalation timer: 10m until next escalation.
alice: noted. keeping paged folks updated.

[~45 minutes later]
ben: all wgpu nodes restarted and healthy. error rate back to baseline (0.8%). routing pref confirmed stable.
dave: reverting eu preference back to normal:
```
rctl set-routing --service=synth-watchdog --prefer-region=none
```
ben: routing reverted. monitor shows normal distribution and healthy latencies.
alice: closing PD incident.
pagerduty: PD-8491 resolved by alice.
carla: creating incident ticket INC-2026-03-14-watchdog-synth. owners: ben (technical), carla (impact/comms), emma (postmortem).
sasha: ACME notified, they acknowledged and will retry jobs. no escalation requested.
emma: I'll draft a postmortem, include timeline, root cause (KV cache / rollout mismatch), mitigation (rolling restarts, routing failover), and follow-ups (metric + rollout gating). tagging ops & infra teams.
alice: thanks everyone. dave, take the rest of the handoff and any overnight watch items.
dave: will do. I'll add notes to the doc and follow up in the AM.
